epics.title: SHA-256 Document Upload Deduplication & Legacy Duplicate Merge
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator uploads a PDF or normative file to CRIE, I want the system to deduplicate uploads by content SHA-256 and merge legacy duplicates while preserving all extracted links, so that the document registry stays clean and previously extracted records can be reviewed instead of duplicated.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0% duplicate document rows created on identical re-upload and 100% relational link retention across merged legacy IDs 1, 10, and 11
epics.tocConstraintRef: Legacy duplicate merge integrity and deterministic SHA-256 matching across re-encoded or renamed PDF uploads
requirements: R1: Add content_sha256 column with indexed lookup plus normalized filename and extracted text-size metadata to the SQLite documents table in crie_document_engine.py, backfilling hashes for existing records.
R2: Compute deterministic SHA-256 content hashes and normalized filename plus text-length fallback checks during document ingestion in crie_document_engine.py before inserting any new document row.
R3: Reject unreadable, empty, or corrupted uploaded files with an explicit validation error before creating partial database rows, preserving the user's upload context.

R4: Update the upload endpoint in crie_assistant_api.py so a matching document returns HTTP 200 with deduplicated=true, the canonical existing document ID, all extracted structured records (enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, rup_curricula) linked to that ID, and an actionable prompt to update or correct existing data instead of inserting a duplicate.

R5: Provide an idempotent, transactional migration script that merges existing duplicate documents (IDs 1, 10, and 11) into a single canonical record, re-pointing all foreign keys and structured record links without orphan rows or data loss.

R6: Surface deduplication feedback in the upload UI showing the matched existing document ID, summary of extracted records, and a direct control to inspect or correct those records without losing context.
R7: Verify hash computation, invalid-file rejection, API deduplication response, and the ID 1/10/11 merge migration across unit, integration, and end-to-end tests using authentic CRIE PDF fixtures.
